stories.headline: BP's Profits Soar on "War Bonus"
stories.summary: Big oil is, well, getting bigger. BP just reported a whopping $5.7 billion profit, their highest since 2022, largely thanks to those sky-high oil prices pushed up by geopolitical tensions (read: the Iran war). Environmental groups are, predictably, not thrilled, calling it "profiteering," while even Trump is grumbling that energy giants are making "too much money."

stories.headline: Trump Media Is Charging Wall Street for Early Tweets
stories.summary: Remember Truth Social? Turns out, Trump's media company has a new, rather controversial, revenue stream: selling early access to market-moving social posts. Wall Street firms can now pay up to $1.2 million a year for a split-second head start on posts that can, and often do, shake global markets. Talk about an exclusive club.

stories.headline: Jeff Bezos Sells $4 Billion in Amazon Stock
stories.summary: When the boss sells, people notice. Jeff Bezos just filed to offload $4 billion worth of Amazon shares. This comes after Amazon's stock hit an all-time high, extending gains from last week's stellar quarterly results. He's probably just diversifying, but it's a hefty chunk of change to move.

stories.headline: Palantir's AI-Fueled Boom
stories.summary: Palantir is having a moment, with its stock jumping 20% after reporting "otherworldly" commercial revenue. Their CEO, Alex Karp, wasn't shy about it, taking a swipe at competitors by saying his customers "declined to become vassal states of the language labs." Basically, their AI platforms are in high demand, and they're making bank.

stories.headline: Gatwick Airport Gets Greenlight for Second Runway
stories.summary: Good news for travelers (maybe, eventually) and bad news for campaigners: Gatwick Airport just won a legal battle to develop its second runway. This £2.2 billion project means about 100,000 more flights a year will be able to use Britain’s second busiest airport, pushing through despite environmental and local opposition.

stories.headline: Iran Peace Talks Are a Head-Scratcher
stories.summary: President Trump made headlines saying he called off strikes on Iran over a "potential deal." But here's the kicker: Iran has since denied any active peace talks, calling Trump's "imminent" deal elusive. So, did we almost have a breakthrough or was it just a bit of wishful thinking? The Strait of Hormuz remains a very tense topic, even if the US Treasury Secretary is talking to Iranians.

stories.headline: Cubans Are Trading the US for Brazil for Asylum
stories.summary: For years, the US was the dream destination for Cubans seeking a new life. But with legal pathways largely closed, a growing number are now heading to Brazil for asylum instead. It's a significant shift in migration patterns, showing how closed doors in one place simply redirect the flow elsewhere.

stories.headline: The US Steps In to Bolster the Japanese Yen
stories.summary: In a move that sounds like something out of a financial thriller, the US dollar weakened against the Japanese yen after both countries confirmed they intervened in markets. The goal? To help shore up Japan's currency. This is a big deal because it signals global economic cooperation to maintain stability, especially for a major economy like Japan's.

stories.headline: Europe's Dry Danube Is Threatening Nuclear Power
stories.summary: Climate change is hitting critical infrastructure. Low water levels in the Danube River are causing big problems for nuclear power plants in Romania and Hungary. Hungary's Paks plant is operating at just 10% capacity because it can't get enough cooling water, and Romania is even blowing up rock outcrops to try and improve water flow. Talk about a desperate measure.

stories.headline: Udhayanidhi Stalin Briefly Detained, Then Released
stories.summary: In a bit of political drama, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin was arrested over some "objectionable remarks," questioned, and then quickly released on station bail by the Madras High Court. The Tamil Nadu government assured the court he wouldn't be remanded in judicial custody. A quick kerfuffle, but a reminder of the ever-present political tensions.

stories.headline: Reels and AI Are Reshaping How Indians Travel
stories.summary: Forget guidebooks – now, it's all about the 'gram! Social media reels and AI are fundamentally changing how Indians plan their trips, from discovering destinations to booking logistics. So next time you're scrolling through a travel reel, remember, you're part of a massive trend.

stories.headline: Tiruchi Aims to Become a Global Tech Hub
stories.summary: Tiruchi, traditionally known for manufacturing, is making a push to become a global capability center. With its strong infrastructure, skilled professionals, and good connectivity, industry leaders believe it has all the ingredients to attract more tech and business service investments. Keep an eye on it – could be the next big thing.

stories.headline: Can PM Modi Reconnect with Gen Z?
stories.summary: Recent student protests have exposed a growing disconnect between PM Narendra Modi's BJP party and young Indians. Experts are now openly questioning if Modi can truly bridge this gap. While Instagram reels might help, it's clear the party has some work to do to win over the younger demographic.

stories.headline: Xbox Owners Can't Play Disc Games During Outage
stories.summary: Here's a fun one: during a recent Xbox outage, many users couldn't play games they *owned on disc*. This highlights a major frustration with digital rights management (DRM) – even if you physically own a game, you might still need to connect to a server to verify it. It’s a stark reminder that "owning" a game isn't what it used to be.

stories.headline: Spotify Hits 300 Million Subscribers, Despite Price Hikes
stories.summary: Turns out, people really love their music (and podcasts). Spotify announced they now have over 300 million subscribers, a 9% jump in the last quarter, even after raising prices in several regions. Goes to show, if your service is good enough, people will pay.

stories.headline: AI-Generated Images Are Making Blogs Less Readable
stories.summary: You know those slightly-off, uncanny valley images that pop up in articles? Turns out, people are really starting to hate them. A new blog post (ironically, probably without AI images) suggests that AI-generated images actually discourage people from reading your blog. Authenticity, it seems, still wins.

stories.headline: The Next Xbox Could Play *Every* Xbox Game Ever
stories.summary: Hold onto your retro controllers! Leaked memos suggest that the next Xbox, codenamed Project Helix, could potentially play every single Xbox game ever made – from the original 2001 console to the latest titles, plus PC games. If true, it would give the console an unprecedented library and a huge nostalgia boost.

stories.headline: Airtable's Valuation Takes a Dive in Acquisition
stories.summary: Remember Airtable, the spreadsheet-database hybrid once valued at a sky-high $11 billion in 2021? Well, it's just been acquired by Bending Spoons for $1.28 billion. That's a massive drop and a stark reminder of the often-volatile nature of tech valuations in today's market.

stories.headline: Life's Purpose Is More Complex Than You Think
stories.summary: Ever ponder the meaning of life? Philosopher Alan Love suggests that purpose isn't just a human-centric idea. From birds faking broken wings to protect their young to cancer cells pursuing their own 'agency,' he argues that purpose, function, and goal-directedness are observed throughout nature. It challenges us to think beyond our personal "calling."

stories.headline: Forgotten Keys to a Scientific Golden Age
stories.summary: As the US debates its scientific future, an analysis points out three "forgotten" keys for fostering a true scientific golden age. Beyond just funding, it delves into elements like collaboration, long-term vision, and nurturing diverse talent, suggesting that getting "doing science" right is more nuanced than it seems.

stories.headline: Ukraine's Cheap Drones Get Smart with US AI
stories.summary: This is a game-changer for modern warfare: a US company has inked a $100 million deal to give 50,000 Ukrainian kamikaze drones advanced AI capabilities. This means these relatively cheap drones can now track targets on their own, making them significantly more effective. It's a stark example of AI's direct and impactful role in conflict zones.

stories.headline: AI-Supervised Exam Disaster: 58,000 Students Retake
stories.summary: Talk about a learning curve! An AI-supervised remote exam went so spectacularly wrong that 58,000 students were forced to retake it. Top scores increased five-fold, indicating something was seriously off with the AI's proctoring or assessment. It's a cautionary tale about deploying AI in sensitive areas like education without thorough vetting.

stories.headline: AWS Is Bringing "Vibe-Coding" AI to Private Clouds
stories.summary: AWS is now allowing Superblocks, a "vibe-coding" tool (which sounds cool, right?), to be embedded into the private clouds of its customers. This is a big step towards decoupling applications from AI models, essentially letting developers bring powerful AI tools closer to their data, making custom AI integration much easier and more secure.

stories.headline: The Quest to Give AI "Taste" Gets $7.9 Million
stories.summary: A startup called Design Arena just raised $7.9 million with a fascinating goal: to bring "taste" to AI models. Their platform is used by millions of people who provide critical human evaluations, essentially teaching AI what's "good" or "bad" design, art, or content. It highlights the crucial role humans still play in refining AI's output beyond just raw data.
